metadata.title: Efficient Decision-Making by Volume-Conserving Physical Object

extraction_notes.note: The paper has no section headings before the Acknowledgement, so every node has an empty section; two equations share the label eq:cond1 (Eqs. 6 and 7).
Typos in the source kept verbatim: E(S) = (mu_A + mu_B) N should be a difference; N_N stands for N_B.
Table 1 (the per-machine estimates used in Eqs. 11-12) is a table, not a fact; its entries are only referenced by DP5.
TOW dynamics is typed algorithm with origin external (Kim et al.), although the conclusion says 'we proposed TOW dynamics'; the same authors introduced it in the cited prior work.

metadata.extraction_comment: The argument is a chain of short derivations in running text without proof environments, so results are prose claims linked by inferred uses edges rather than proof nodes.

nodes.statement: Kim et al. proposed an MBP solution using a dynamical system, called ``tug-of-war (TOW) dynamics''; this algorithm was inspired by the spatiotemporal dynamics of a single-celled amoeboid organism (the true slime mold P. polycephalum), which maintains a constant intracellular-resource volume while collecting environmental information by concurrently expanding and shrinking its pseudopod-like terminal parts.
nodes.raw_latex: Kim et al. proposed an MBP solution using a dynamical system, called ``tug-of-war (TOW) dynamics''; this algorithm was inspired by the spatiotemporal dynamics of a single-celled amoeboid organism (the true slime mold {\it P. polycephalum})~\cite{kim1,kim2,kim3,kim4,kim5,kim6}, which maintains a constant intracellular-resource volume while collecting environmental information by concurrently expanding and shrinking its pseudopod-like terminal parts.
nodes.clean_text: Kim et al. proposed an MBP solution using a dynamical system, called ``tug-of-war (TOW) dynamics''; this algorithm was inspired by the spatiotemporal dynamics of a single-celled amoeboid organism (the true slime mold P. polycephalum), which maintains a constant intracellular-resource volume while collecting environmental information by concurrently expanding and shrinking its pseudopod-like terminal parts.

nodes.statement: In our previous studies, we showed that, owing to the nonlocal correlation derived from the volume-conservation law, TOW dynamics exhibit higher performance than other well-known algorithms such as the modified epsilon-greedy algorithm and the modified softmax algorithm, which is comparable to the UCB1-tuned algorithm (seen as the best choice among parameter-free algorithms).
conclusions: In our previous studies, we showed that, owing to the nonlocal correlation derived from the volume-conservation law, TOW dynamics exhibit higher performance than other well-known algorithms such as the modified epsilon-greedy algorithm and the modified softmax algorithm, which is comparable to the UCB1-tuned algorithm (seen as the best choice among parameter-free algorithms).
nodes.raw_latex: In our previous studies~\cite{kim1,kim2,kim3,kim4,kim5,kim6}, we showed that, owing to the nonlocal correlation derived from the volume-conservation law, TOW dynamics exhibit higher performance than other well-known algorithms such as the modified $\epsilon$-greedy algorithm and the modified softmax algorithm, which is comparable to the UCB1-tuned algorithm (seen as the best choice among parameter-free algorithms~\cite{auer}).

nodes.statement: E(N_B) & = & Sigma_t=0^N-1 Q(phi sqrtt) nonumber \\ & leq & Sigma_t=0^N-1 frac12 exp(-fracphi^22 t) nonumber \\ & = & frac12 + Sigma_t=1^N-1 frac12 exp(-fracphi^22 t) nonumber \\ & leq & frac12 + int_0^N-1 frac12 exp(-fracphi^22 t) dt nonumber \\ & = & frac12 - frac1phi^2 left( exp(-fracphi^22(N-1)) - 1 right) \\ & rightarrow & frac12 + frac1phi^2 .
nodes.raw_latex:
\begin{eqnarray}
E(N_B) & = & \Sigma_{t=0}^{N-1} {\bf Q}(\phi \sqrt{t}) \nonumber \\
       & \leq & \Sigma_{t=0}^{N-1} \frac{1}{2} \exp(-\frac{\phi^2}{2} t) \nonumber \\
       & = & \frac{1}{2} + \Sigma_{t=1}^{N-1} \frac{1}{2} \exp(-\frac{\phi^2}{2} t) \nonumber \\
       & \leq & \frac{1}{2} + \int_{0}^{N-1} \frac{1}{2} \exp(-\frac{\phi^2}{2} t) dt \nonumber \\
       & = & \frac{1}{2} - \frac{1}{\phi^2} \left( \exp(-\frac{\phi^2}{2}(N-1))  - 1  \right) \\
       & \rightarrow & \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{\phi^2} .
\end{eqnarray}
